title: A National Campaign to Restrict Voting

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日时事通讯 DealBook 的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的现场，采访商界、政界和文化界最具影响力的几位领袖，其中包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上直播精选采访，任何人都可以免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序来观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 我希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, in the weeks after the 2020 election, Georgia's Republican leaders were seen as defenders of election integrity,
sentences.zh: 今天，在 2020 年大选结束后的几周里，佐治亚州的共和党领导人被视为选举公正的捍卫者，

sentences.en: repeatedly rebuffing demands by President Trump to overturn Joe Biden's victory.
sentences.zh: 他们多次回绝了特朗普总统推翻乔·拜登胜利果实的诉求。

sentences.en: Now, after adopting a sweeping election law, they've emerged as a threat to voting rights.
sentences.zh: 现在，在通过了一项严厉的选举法后，他们却成了投票权的威胁。

sentences.en: So, Nick, what is the story of how Georgia came to pass this sweeping new election law?
sentences.zh: 那么，尼克，佐治亚州通过这项意义深远的新选举法的前因后果是怎样的？

sentences.en: Well, I think you have to look at these hearings that were held in the Georgia legislature back in mid to late December.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为你必须回顾一下佐治亚州议会在 12 月中下旬举行的这些听证会。

sentences.en: As the president was going around looking for people to support his claims and falsehoods about the election
sentences.zh: 当时总统到处寻找支持他对大选的说法和虚假指控的人，

sentences.en: and was constantly getting rebuffed by statewide election officials like the secretary of state, he found a lot of allies in the state legislature.
sentences.zh: 并且不断遭到国务卿等全州选举官员的拒绝，于是他在州议会里找到了很多盟友。

sentences.en: The state of Georgia is one of the Republican trifecta states where both houses of the state legislature, as well as the governorship, is held by Republicans.
sentences.zh: 佐治亚州是共和党三权包揽的州之一，州议会两院以及州长职位均由共和党人把持。

sentences.en: And so what they did is they held these hearings where they invited people like Rudy Giuliani
sentences.zh: 因此，他们采取的做法是举行听证会，邀请鲁迪·朱利安尼等人

sentences.en: to testify to kind of prove his points that there was lots of fraud, lots of issues with the election.
sentences.zh: 前去作证，以期证明他的观点，即选举中存在大量舞弊和诸多问题。

sentences.en: And in those hearings, Giuliani in particular said some pretty inflammatory things, casting about a bunch of conspiracy theories, falsehoods about the elections,
sentences.zh: 在那些听证会上，朱利安尼尤其发表了一些相当煽动性的言论，散布了一堆阴谋论和关于选举的虚假言论，

sentences.en: falsehood about the company that provided the elections machines to Georgia.
sentences.zh: 以及关于向佐治亚州提供投票机的公司的谎言。

sentences.en: And it was in those meetings that I think you started to see a legislature, see an opportunity to seize on this moment and this doubt that had been cast among the Republican base
sentences.zh: 正是在这些会议上，我认为你开始看到议会看到了一个机会，想要抓住这个时刻以及共和党基层对选举结果产生的怀疑，

sentences.en: about the results of the election to possibly do something with the state's election laws.
sentences.zh: 从而对该州的选举法律做点文章。

sentences.en: And why exactly is that, given just how little fraud was ever documented in Georgia in the 2020 election?
sentences.zh: 鉴于 2020 年佐治亚州大选中记录在案的舞弊行为少之又少，这究竟是为什么呢？

sentences.en: Why would these Republican lawmakers seize on this mostly false message from President Trump
sentences.zh: 为什么这些共和党议员要抓住来自特朗普总统以及像鲁迪·朱利安尼这样的人的这种基本属于虚假的信息，

sentences.en: and people like Rudy Giuliani and start to run with it and try to come up with a plan to remedy it?
sentences.zh: 并开始顺着它推波助澜，试图想出一个补救计划呢？

sentences.en: Well, publicly, what the lawmakers were saying was that there was now a crisis of confidence within the electorate.
sentences.zh: 嗯，公开来看，议员们当时的说法是，选民中现在出现了信任危机。

sentences.en: There were a lot of people, particularly their supporters, who had bought into a lot of the lies and the falsehoods that were told about the 2020 election,
sentences.zh: 有很多人，尤其是他们的支持者，相信了许多关于 2020 年大选的谎言和虚假信息，

sentences.en: some in which they might have helped spread by holding some of these hearings.
sentences.zh: 其中有些谎言他们自己可能也通过举行这些听证会起到了传播的作用。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that therefore something needed to be done.
sentences.zh: 因此必须采取一些措施。

sentences.en: But I think you also need to look at the political reality that is on the ground in Georgia right now.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得你还得看看佐治亚州目前的政治现实。

sentences.en: It had been a reliably Republican state at the statewide level for years.
sentences.zh: 多年来，它在全州层面上一直是可靠的共和党阵地。

sentences.en: And then in 2018, Stacey Abrams, the Democratic candidate for governor, only lost by about 50,000 votes.
sentences.zh: 然后到了 2018 年，民主党州长候选人斯黛西·艾布拉姆斯仅以大约 5 万票之差落败。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it was a really close election.
sentences.zh: 那是一场非常惊险的选举。

sentences.en: Fast forward to 2020, Biden carries the state as a presidential candidate for Democrats for the first time in decades.
sentences.zh: 快进到 2020 年，作为民主党总统候选人的拜登几十年来首次在该州胜出。

sentences.en: And then you have the two United States senators, both Republican incumbents, who are now facing runoff elections by two Democratic challengers.
sentences.zh: 接着你又有两位美国参议员，都是共和党现任议员，现在正面临两位民主党挑战者的决选。

sentences.en: And both of those elections at this point in December, you know, are way too close to call.
sentences.zh: 而且在 12 月这个时间点，这两场选举可以说是难分伯仲。

sentences.en: They're basically dead even.
sentences.zh: 基本上是不相上下。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So you have a Republican legislature that is looking at this state that had once been reliably read just turning more and more purple.
sentences.zh: 所以你有一个共和党议会，正看着这个曾经稳如磐石的红色州变得越来越紫。

sentences.en: And so they view this political reality and they see maybe an opportunity to change some of these voting laws.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们审视这种政治现实，看到或许可以借此机会修改部分投票法律。

sentences.en: So, Nick,
sentences.zh: 所以，尼克，

sentences.en: it sounds like President Trump and those around him are giving voice in this moment and perhaps cover to pre-existing electoral anxieties among Georgia Republican lawmakers who are starting to fear that they're losing total control of power in Georgia.
sentences.zh: 听起来特朗普总统和周围的人在此时发出了声音，也许是为佐治亚州共和党议员中原本就存在的选举焦虑提供了掩护，他们开始担心自己会彻底失去在佐治亚州的权力。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: The Republican legislators in Georgia know very well just how changing voting laws and restricting access to voting can impact their ability to hold on to power.
sentences.zh: 佐治亚州的共和党议员非常清楚，修改投票法以及限制投票权会如何影响他们保住权力的能力。

sentences.en: It's a state that has a history of restrictive voting laws that date back to the Reconstruction era.
sentences.zh: 这是一个有着可以追溯到重建时期的限制性投票法历史的州。

sentences.en: And even most recently, after the Voting Rights Act was guided by the Supreme Court in 2013, had enacted numerous different laws that severely restricted voting.
sentences.zh: 就在最近，2013 年最高法院掏空《选举权法》之后，该州也颁布了许多严重限制投票的不同法律。

sentences.en: You had purges of voter rolls for inactive voters.
sentences.zh: 比如针对不活跃选民的选民名册清洗。

sentences.en: There was at one point 500,000 that were just knocked off in one single day in July of 2017.
sentences.zh: 曾在 2017 年 7 月的某一天一口气剔除了 50 万人。

sentences.en: And there have been over 200 voting precincts that have been shuttered since 2012.
sentences.zh: 自 2012 年以来，已有超过 200 个投票站被关闭。

sentences.en: Majority of those impacting communities of color.
sentences.zh: 其中大部分都冲击到了有色人种社区。

sentences.en: So,
sentences.zh: 所以，

sentences.en: there is a history of changes to voting laws creating new barriers to the ballot box in Georgia that have often been used by Republican legislators to kind of help hold on to power amid shifting electorates.
sentences.zh: 在佐治亚州，修改投票法从而为投票箱制造新障碍的历史一直存在，在选民结构发生变化的情况下，共和党议员经常利用这些来帮助保住权力。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then in January, not that many weeks after those hearings you just described, those two Republican senators in Georgia go on to lose their seats to two Democratic challengers.
sentences.zh: 然后到了 1 月，就在你刚描述的那些听证会结束几周后，佐治亚州的那两位共和党参议员在决选中输给了两位民主党挑战者。

sentences.en: And I have to imagine that deepens the sense of crisis among Republican state lawmakers in Georgia.
sentences.zh: 我想这一定加深了佐治亚州共和党州议员的危机感。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: In the arc of history, Georgia almost turns blue overnight.
sentences.zh: 在历史的长河中，佐治亚州几乎一夜之间变成了蓝色。

sentences.en: Biden wins the state in November.
sentences.zh: 拜登在 11 月赢下了该州。

sentences.en: John Ossoff and Raphael Warnock win their Senate runoff elections in January.
sentences.zh: 乔恩·奥索夫和拉斐尔·沃诺克在 1 月赢得了参议员决选。

sentences.en: And the Republican state legislature realizes that if they're going to make changes, they're going to have to move quickly.
sentences.zh: 共和党州议会意识到，如果他们要做出改变，就必须迅速行动。

sentences.en: So, what do they do?
sentences.zh: 那么，他们做了什么？

sentences.en: So, what happens is over the kind of month of January, they're meeting with different groups.
sentences.zh: 所以，发生的情况是，在整个 1 月份，他们一直在与不同的团体开会。

sentences.en: They're talking to their constituents.
sentences.zh: 他们与选民交谈。

sentences.en: And then all of a sudden, about 80 bills and resolutions are just unfurled.
sentences.zh: 然后突然之间，大约 80 项法案和决议就被一股脑儿地抛了出来。

sentences.en: 80 bills.
sentences.zh: 80 项法案。

sentences.en: 80 different bills and resolutions.
sentences.zh: 80 项不同的法案和决议。

sentences.en: All varying degrees of trying to restrict access to voting.
sentences.zh: 全都从不同程度上试图限制投票权。

sentences.en: Some very strident.
sentences.zh: 有些非常严厉。

sentences.en: Some dealing with very minute things.
sentences.zh: 有些涉及非常细微的事情。

sentences.en: But they all just kind of unfurl in the legislature in late January and early February.
sentences.zh: 但它们都在 1 月下旬和 2 月初一股脑儿地呈现在议会面前。

sentences.en: Tell me about the most strident of these proposals.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲其中最严厉的几项提案吧。

sentences.en: Well, one of these proposals specifically looked to restrict early voting on the weekends, in particular on Sunday.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其中一项提案专门旨在限制周末的提前投票，特别是周日。

sentences.en: And voting on Sunday is an incredibly popular and important part of voting within the black church known as Souls to the Polls.
sentences.zh: 而在周日投票是黑人教会中一项极受欢迎且极其重要的投票传统，被称为“灵魂奔向投票箱”（Souls to the Polls）。

sentences.en: And, you know, the black church is such an important part of the black community, particularly in Georgia.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，黑人教会是黑人社区非常重要的一部分，尤其是在佐治亚州。

sentences.en: And for years, they have just been increasing their role in civic engagement and getting more and more of the black community able to vote, helping them to vote,
sentences.zh: 多年来，他们不断扩大自己在公民参与中的作用，让越来越多的黑人社区能够投票、帮助他们投票，

sentences.en: bringing them to vote.
sentences.zh: 带他们去投票。

sentences.en: And so, this provision was seen at almost specifically targeting those churches to prevent them from helping, you know, large parts of the black community from voting on Sunday.
sentences.zh: 因此，这项条款被视为几乎是专门针对这些教会，以防止他们帮助黑人社区的大部分人在周日投票。

sentences.en: So, this is clearly aimed at weakening the power of Georgia's black electorate, which is heavily Democratic.
sentences.zh: 所以，这显然是为了削弱佐治亚州黑人选民的力量，而黑人选民主要是民主党的支持者。

sentences.en: No question.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问。

sentences.en: And so, what is the reaction to that proposal?
sentences.zh: 那么，外界对该提案的反应是什么？

sentences.en: It's immediately met with outrage, both within Georgia and nationally.
sentences.zh: 它立即在佐治亚州乃至全国引发了愤怒。

sentences.en: And eventually, the Republicans backed off that measure.
sentences.zh: 最终，共和党人从这项措施上退让了。

sentences.en: So, Nick, what proposals do end up in this final package of legislation?
sentences.zh: 那么，尼克，最终打包的立法方案里到底包含了哪些提案？

sentences.en: Well, let me give you a few examples.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我给你举几个例子。

sentences.en: But broadly, they deal with absentee voting, with drop boxes, with voting in person, and with election oversight.
sentences.zh: 但总体而言，它们涉及缺席投票、投票箱、现场投票以及选举监督。

sentences.en: So, when it comes to absentee voting, one big change is that an ID is now required.
sentences.zh: 因此，就缺席投票而言，一个重大的变化是现在必须提供身份证件。

sentences.en: Basically, anyone who wants to request an absentee ballot will need to show a driver's license or a state ID number instead of just doing a signature,
sentences.zh: 基本上，任何想要申请缺席选票的人都需要出示驾照或州身份证号码，而不仅仅是签个名，

sentences.en: which was then matched on a file and created a host of issues.
sentences.zh: 以前签名会与档案进行核对，这引发了一系列问题。

sentences.en: So, Republicans argued that bringing in these IDs made it both secure and a little easier.
sentences.zh: 因此，共和党人认为，引入这些身份证件既能保证安全，又能简化流程。

sentences.en: At the same time, civil rights groups will point that anytime you add an ID requirement to voting,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，民权组织则指出，每当你给投票增加身份证件要求时，

sentences.en: it normally disproportionately impacts communities of color and poorer communities.
sentences.zh: 它通常会对有色人种社区和贫困社区造成不成比例的影响。

sentences.en: So, therefore, introducing identification requirements make it harder for them to vote.
sentences.zh: 因此，引入身份识别要求使得他们投票变得更难了。

sentences.en: Okay, got it.
sentences.zh: 好的，明白了。

sentences.en: What else?
sentences.zh: 还有什么？

sentences.en: They're also going to ban state and local election officials, as well as third-party groups, from sending out absentee ballot applications.
sentences.zh: 他们还将禁止州和地方选举官员以及第三方团体分发缺席选票申请表。

sentences.en: This was done a lot in the 2020 election to kind of encourage people who weren't familiar with absentee voting to know that they had the ability to.
sentences.zh: 这在 2020 年大选中被大量使用，旨在鼓励那些不熟悉缺席投票的人知道他们拥有这种权利。

sentences.en: They're going to limit drop boxes, which is where a voter can come and drop off their filled-out absentee ballot during the 2020 election.
sentences.zh: 他们将限制投票箱的数量，选民可以在 2020 年大选期间来到投票箱前投入填好的缺席选票。

sentences.en: Those were open 24-7.
sentences.zh: 当时那些投票箱是 24 小时开放的。

sentences.en: They were just kind of outside, and you could bring it there.
sentences.zh: 它们就摆在室外，你可以直接拿去投。

sentences.en: The new law will limit the amount of drop boxes to just one per 100,000 active voters in a county, and then also it will force them to be brought inside offices,
sentences.zh: 新法案将把投票箱的数量限制为一个县每 10 万名活跃选民只能设一个，并且还将强制将它们搬到办公室内部，

sentences.en: meaning that they're no longer a 24-7 option.
sentences.zh: 这意味着它们不再是 24 小时开放的选择了。

sentences.en: Instead, they're going to have much more restrictive hours as to when the building is open.
sentences.zh: 相反，根据大楼开放的时间，它们的开放时间将受到更严格的限制。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哈。

sentences.en: Yeah, and then there's a whole host of new proposals that deal with oversight of elections and who gets to run elections and what kind of power the Secretary of State has.
sentences.zh: 是的，还有一大堆关于选举监督、谁来负责选举以及国务卿拥有何种权力的全新提案。

sentences.en: It's over the state that just kind of will alter and basically give more power to the state legislature over the administration and governance of elections.
sentences.zh: 这关乎全州，将会改变并基本上赋予州议会更多关于选举管理和治理的权力。

sentences.en: But there's this one other proposal that has gotten a lot of attention, and that's basically Georgia is known for having very long lines when it comes to in-person voting.
sentences.zh: 但还有另一个引起广泛关注的提案，那就是佐治亚州历来以现场投票排队时间极长而闻名。

sentences.en: Sometimes they stretch for hours.
sentences.zh: 有时队伍会绵延数小时之久。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Now, lines tend to stretch longer in poorer communities and urban areas,
sentences.zh: 如今，排队的时间往往在贫困社区和城市地区更长，

sentences.en: and so there's been third-party groups that will sometimes come and bring food and water to those people who are waiting in line for hours on end in the blistering Georgia heat.
sentences.zh: 因此会有第三方团体有时会赶来，给那些在佐治亚州酷热中排队数小时的人们提供食物和水。

sentences.en: Now, this law would ban those groups from bringing food and water and other assistance to voters waiting in hours-long lines.
sentences.zh: 现在，这项法律将禁止这些团体向在长达数小时的队伍中等待的选民提供食物、水和其他援助。

sentences.en: Nick, that proposal seems very hard to understand as anything other than an attempt to make it harder for certain people to vote.
sentences.zh: 尼克，除了企图让某些人更难投票之外，这个提案似乎很难被理解为其他任何东西。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: And so how do the people who proposed that defend it?
sentences.zh: 那么提出这项提案的人是如何为之辩护的呢？

sentences.en: There hasn't been that much of a defense except that they've tried to say technically it's just there's a radius of 150 feet that, you know, this ban affects.
sentences.zh: 并没有多少实质性的辩护，他们只是试图从技术层面说，这项禁令影响的仅仅是一个 150 英尺的半径范围。

sentences.en: And so it gets into this kind of technicality, and that's where the defense has been.
sentences.zh: 因此它陷入了这种类似钻牛角尖的技术细节，而他们的辩护就是基于此。

sentences.en: But the reality is it's going to prevent help, assistance, and resources from reaching voters who are waiting in line to vote.
sentences.zh: 但现实是，这将阻止援助、帮助和资源送达那些排队等待投票的选民手中。

sentences.en: So once this final package is complete and it's introduced, how intensely is this debated in a Republican-controlled legislature?
sentences.zh: 那么，一旦这个最终打包方案完成并被推出，在由共和党控制的议会中它受到了多大程度的激烈辩论？

sentences.en: My sense is that it's kind of fate accompli.
sentences.zh: 我的感觉是这有点像是既成事实。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: So once they arrived on a final package of proposals, it moved very quickly.
sentences.zh: 因此，一旦他们就最终的提案包达成一致，进展就非常快。

sentences.en: The hour of convening having arrived, all members of the House will please report to their assigned seats.
sentences.zh: 集合的时间已经到了，请众议院全体成员回到各自指定的座位。

sentences.en: The clerk will ring the bell.
sentences.zh: 书记员将摇铃。

sentences.en: On Thursday, both chambers of the state legislature set about for a final passage.
sentences.zh: 周四，州议会两院开始为最终通过做准备。

sentences.en: And though it was going to pass probably along party line votes, they had to leave it open for debate.
sentences.zh: 尽管它可能会沿着党派划线投票获得通过，但他们还是必须留出辩论的空间。

sentences.en: I rise today in opposition to the voter suppression bill otherwise known as SB 202.
sentences.zh: 我今天站在这里，反对这项被称为 SB 202 的压制选民法案。

sentences.en: And what happened on Thursday was a lot of Democratic lawmakers stood up and gave pretty impassioned speeches against the bill.
sentences.zh: 周四发生的事情是，许多民主党议员站起来发表了相当充满激情的演讲，反对该法案。

sentences.en: We will not stand idly by and let Jim Crow 2.0 roll back the clock on our new Georgia.
sentences.zh: 我们绝不会袖手旁观，任由“吉姆·克劳 2.0”让我们的新佐治亚州开历史倒车。

sentences.en: Mr. Speaker, thank you.
sentences.zh: 议长先生，谢谢您。

sentences.en: I yield the well.
sentences.zh: 我让出发言席。

sentences.en: They invoked the state's long history of repressive and racially targeted voting laws and connected these current restrictions to that long history.
sentences.zh: 他们提及了该州压制性和针对种族的投票法的悠久历史，并将当前的这些限制措施与那段悠久历史联系起来。

sentences.en: But it's time to take a chill pill, folks.
sentences.zh: 但是伙计们，是时候冷静一下了。

sentences.en: Republicans stood up and intended more to push back on those attacks than necessarily offer any other defense.
sentences.zh: 共和党人站起来，更多是意在回击这些攻击，而非提供任何其他的辩护。

sentences.en: It's time to read the bill.
sentences.zh: 是时候读一读法案了。

sentences.en: Don't just listen to what you're being told.
sentences.zh: 不要只听别人对你说了什么。

sentences.en: Actually, read the bill.
sentences.zh: 去好好读读法案。

sentences.en: Show me where there's suppression.
sentences.zh: 指给我看哪里有压制。

sentences.en: There is no suppression in this bill.
sentences.zh: 这项法案中根本没有压制。

sentences.en: Other than pointing to that the bill was designed to improve election security and, quote unquote, restore confidence within the electorate.
sentences.zh: 除了指出该法案旨在改善选举安全以及所谓“恢复选民信心”之外。

sentences.en: The ayes are 100.
sentences.zh: 赞成票 100 票。

sentences.en: The nays are 75.
sentences.zh: 反对票 75 票。

sentences.en: This bill having received.
sentences.zh: 鉴于本法案已获得……

sentences.en: After they passed the bill along party line votes in both chambers, they sent the bill quickly over to Governor Kemp, who was poised to sign it.
sentences.zh: 在两院通过党派划线投票通过该法案后，他们迅速将法案送交准备签署的肯普州长。

sentences.en: He held a signing ceremony behind closed doors late on Thursday night.
sentences.zh: 周四深夜，他在闭门情况下签署了一份法案。

sentences.en: But in a final moment of protest, one of the Democratic lawmakers, Park Cannon, who is a young black woman, came to attend the signing just to view it.
sentences.zh: 但在抗议的最后关头，民主党议员之一帕克·坎农——她是一位年轻的黑人女性——来到签署现场，只是为了旁观。

sentences.en: And at one point, she knocked lightly on the door as if, you know, someone were coming to your house.
sentences.zh: 在某一时刻，她轻轻敲了敲门，就像是，你知道的，有人去你家敲门那样。

sentences.en: It wasn't a loud bang.
sentences.zh: 那不是一声巨响。

sentences.en: And she was immediately put in handcuffs and walked away.
sentences.zh: 她随即被戴上手铐带走了。

sentences.en: Are you serious?
sentences.zh: 你是认真的吗？

sentences.en: No, you are not.
sentences.zh: 不，你才不认真。

sentences.en: Represent.
sentences.zh: 说得好。

sentences.en: She's not under arreSt.
sentences.zh: 她没有被捕。

sentences.en: While handcuffed, while a bunch of activists and protesters caught that moment on tape.
sentences.zh: 戴着手铐的时候，一群活动人士和抗议者将那一刻拍了下来。

sentences.en: Cite the violation.
sentences.zh: 指出哪条违规了。

sentences.en: Cite the code.
sentences.zh: 指出法条。

sentences.en: What is she in violation of?
sentences.zh: 她违反了什么？

sentences.en: I want you to cite the code.
sentences.zh: 我要求你指出法条。

sentences.en: Cite the code.
sentences.zh: 指出法条。

sentences.en: Cite the code.
sentences.zh: 指出法条。

sentences.en: Cite the code.
sentences.zh: 指出法条。

sentences.en: And Nick, what is the reaction to this law being so quickly passed and signed into law beyond Georgia?
sentences.zh: 尼克，在佐治亚州之外，对于这项被迅速通过并签署成为法律的法案，大家的反应是什么？

sentences.en: Well, the reaction is almost as swift as the passing,
sentences.zh: 嗯，大家的反应几乎和法案通过的速度一样快。

sentences.en: as Democrats across the country denounce this effort as being harsh and restrictive in creating new barriers to the ballot box.
sentences.zh: 全国各地的民主党人纷纷谴责这一举措严苛且具限制性，为投票箱设置了新的障碍。

sentences.en: President Biden himself called the effort sick and un-American.
sentences.zh: 拜登总统本人称这一举措令人发指、有违美国精神。

sentences.en: And what Biden knows and what Democrats across the country know is that what just happened in Georgia is poised to happen in states across the country.
sentences.zh: 拜登以及全国各地的民主党人都清楚，佐治亚州刚刚发生的事情，很有可能会在全美各州上演。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: So, Nick, if President Biden and fellow Democrats are right to see Georgia as one of many states poised to pass these kinds of voting restrictions,
sentences.zh: 那么，尼克，如果拜登总统和同僚民主党人把佐治亚州视为准备通过此类投票限制措施的众多州之一，这种看法是正确的的话，

sentences.en: where else are we starting to see these measures being introduced?
sentences.zh: 我们开始在哪些地方看到这些措施被提出？

sentences.en: Well, you could almost look at any state across the country for restrictions being introduced.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你几乎可以在全国任何一个州看到有人提出限制措施。

sentences.en: The Brennan Center found that there were more than 250 voting-related bills in 43 different states across the country, and that number might have even gone up since, you know,
sentences.zh: 布伦南中心发现，全国43个不同的州有250多项与投票相关的法案，而且这个数字甚至可能自，你知道的，

sentences.en: the weekend.
sentences.zh: 周末以来有所增加。

sentences.en: But where we're seeing the kind of greatest likelihood of some pretty impactful pieces of legislation moving is in Texas, in Arizona, and in Florida,
sentences.zh: 但我们看到最有可能会通过一些颇具影响力的立法的地方是得克萨斯州、亚利桑那州和佛罗里达州，

sentences.en: three states that also have complete Republican control of both the state legislatures and the governorship.
sentences.zh: 这三个州的州议会和州长职位也都完全由共和党把持。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And three states that are very much like Georgia in that they're battleground states.
sentences.zh: 这三个州在作为摇摆州这一点上非常像佐治亚州。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确切地说。

sentences.en: Florida, the most traditional of all swing states,
sentences.zh: 佛罗里达州是所有摇摆州中最传统的一个，

sentences.en: Texas is like Georgia in that it's experiencing a kind of increasing population shift that's leading it more towards seeing it possibly go purple, if not blue.
sentences.zh: 得克萨斯州和佐治亚州相似，因为它的总人口正不断发生变化，这使得它更有可能变成摇摆州，甚至变成蓝色。

sentences.en: And Arizona, which, like Georgia, did actually turn blue for the first time in years in the presidential election,
sentences.zh: 而亚利桑那州和佐治亚州一样，在这次总统大选中多年来首次变蓝，

sentences.en: and now has two Democratic United States senators for the first time in decades, just like Georgia.
sentences.zh: 并且几十年来首次拥有了两位民主党联邦参议员，就像佐治亚州一样。

sentences.en: So there's a pretty clear pattern starting to emerge here of Republican state lawmakers sensing in these states that their grip on power is loosening and taking action to try to restrict voting in ways that would perhaps allow them to hold on to that power.
sentences.zh: 因此这里开始出现一个相当清晰的模式：这些州的共和党州议员感觉到他们对权力的控制正在松动，于是采取行动试图限制投票，这或许能让他们保住权力。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And you're even seeing some similar proposals that you saw in Georgia appear in other states.
sentences.zh: 你甚至会发现一些你在佐治亚州看到的类似提案也出现在其他州。

sentences.en: In Florida, Republicans there are looking to restrict the availability and utilization of drop boxes.
sentences.zh: 在佛罗里达州，那里的共和党人正试图限制得票收件箱（收集选票的投递箱）的可用性和使用。

sentences.en: In Arizona, Republican lawmakers are looking to basically make it easier for state and local election officials to clean the voter rolls.
sentences.zh: 在亚利桑那州，共和党议员正试图从根本上让州和地方选举官员更容易清理选民名册。

sentences.en: It's known as purging when they can remove voters who weren't active in recent elections from their registration.
sentences.zh: 这被称为清洗，即他们可以从登记册中删除在最近选举中不活跃的选民。

sentences.en: And in Texas, they're bringing a host of proposals that are very similar to Georgia.
sentences.zh: 而在得克萨斯州，他们提出了许多与佐治亚州非常相似的提案。

sentences.en: One is they are imposing an early voting restriction that would limit the hours that early voting is permitted from 6 a.m.
sentences.zh: 其中一项是他们正在强加一项提前投票限制，将允许提前投票的时间限制在早上6点

sentences.en: to 9 p.m., which would essentially ban the 24-hour voting locations that were in Harris County, home to Houston, last November.
sentences.zh: 到晚上9点之间，这基本上等于禁止了去年11月在休斯顿所在的哈里斯县出现的24小时投票点。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Nick, the similarity of these proposals would seem to suggest a fair bit of coordination.
sentences.zh: 尼克，这些提案的相似性似乎表明其中存在相当多的协调。

sentences.en: So what have you found about that?
sentences.zh: 那么你对此有什么发现？

sentences.en: Well, there's multiple groups that are working behind the scenes to push these new voting restrictions.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有多个组织在幕后合作推动这些新的投票限制。

sentences.en: There's conservative groups like the Heritage Foundation, who has publicly taken credit when Georgia's law passed last week.
sentences.zh: 有一些保守派组织，比如传统基金会，当佐治亚州的法律上周通过时，他们公开居功自傲。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And often you'll see laws that very similarly reflect the language in those best practices.
sentences.zh: 通常你会看到法律非常相似地反映了这些最佳实践中的用词。

sentences.en: At the party level, there are two, quote-unquote, election integrity committees,
sentences.zh: 在政党层面，有两个，姑且称之为“选举诚信委员会”，

sentences.en: one within the Republican National Committee and one within the Republican State Leadership Conference, which is the State Legislator Committee.
sentences.zh: 一个在共和党全国委员会内，另一个在共和党州领导层会议内，也就是州议员委员会。

sentences.en: And both of those committees are looking to bring some form of coordination and organization to this effort to restrict voting.
sentences.zh: 这两个委员会都希望为这一限制投票的努力带来某种形式的协调和组织。

sentences.en: The one amongst the Republican state legislatures in particular is hoping to draft what's been described to me as an e-notebook of statutory language, executive orders,
sentences.zh: 特别是共和党州议会当中的那个委员会，希望能起草一份向我描述为包含成文法语言、行政命令的电子笔记本，

sentences.en: anything that's been tested and withstood either court challenges or is just considered a best practice for other states who are looking to bring in new voting restrictions.
sentences.zh: 任何经过测试并经受住法院挑战，或者被认为可供其他寻求引入新投票限制的州参考的最佳实践。

sentences.en: So the idea is that these outside groups and these parts of the Republican Party are going to deliver legislative language to these state legislatures that they know is most likely to pass legal muster and become law.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的想法是，这些外部组织和共和党的部分机构将向这些州议会提供他们知道最有可能通过法律考验并成为法律的立法文本。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确切地说。

sentences.en: But of course, Nick,
sentences.zh: 但当然，尼克，

sentences.en: this larger coordination would seem to undercut the idea that this is some kind of organic state-by-state response to allegations of fraud or fears of fraud by Republican voters.
sentences.zh: 这种更大规模的协调似乎削弱了这样一种观点，即这是一种针对欺诈指控或共和党选民对欺诈的担忧的某种自发的、各州各自为政的反应。

sentences.en: And it raises the prospect that this is actually just a national electoral strategy being pursued by national Republicans.
sentences.zh: 这也引发了一种可能性，即这实际上只是全国共和党人正在奉行的一项全国性选举战略。

sentences.en: In a way, it can actually be both.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，它实际上可以两者兼而有之。

sentences.en: I think what has to be taken into account here is just how core the question of voting rights and questioning the 2020 election has become within the Republican base.
sentences.zh: 我认为这里必须考虑到的是，投票权问题以及对2020年大选的性质疑在共和党基层中变得多么核心。

sentences.en: But it's almost as animating right now as some of the core cultural issues like abortion has been in terms of some of their priorities and what they want to see their legislators focusing on.
sentences.zh: 但它现在几乎和堕胎等核心文化议题一样具有号召力，成为他们的一些优先事项以及他们希望看到议员们关注的焦点。

sentences.en: So if you look at Georgia, where, you know, nearly 80 bills and resolutions were spilled onto the floor relating to voting, there wasn't necessarily much coordination there.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你看看佐治亚州，你知道，那里有近80项与投票有关的法案和决议提交到议会讨论，当时不一定有那么多的协调。

sentences.en: But what I think happens afterwards, and I think what you're seeing across the country,
sentences.zh: 但我认为接下来发生的事情，我认为你正在全国各地看到的是，

sentences.en: is there is now a movement by some of these outside groups and by some of the arms of the Republican Party apparatus so that they don't necessarily lose the momentum and the opportunity that they see here.
sentences.zh: 其中一些外部组织和共和党机器的一些分支现在发起了一场运动，这样他们就不会失去他们在这里看到的势头和机会。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So that leaves us with the inevitable question, will this effort work by Republicans?
sentences.zh: 这就给我们留下了不可避免的问题：共和党人的这一努力会奏效吗？

sentences.en: Do we expect these measures to keep passing in states like Florida and Arizona and Texas, and do we expect them to help Republicans hold on to power?
sentences.zh: 我们预计这些措施会继续在佛罗里达州、亚利桑那州和得克萨斯州等州通过吗？我们预计它们能帮助共和党人保住权力吗？

sentences.en: Well, there's no reason to think that in any of these states where Republicans control both the legislature and the governorship,
sentences.zh: 嗯，没有理由认为在这些共和党既控制议会又控制州长的任何州里，

sentences.en: that they won't continue passing these bills to either restrict voting.
sentences.zh: 他们不会继续通过这些法案来限制投票。

sentences.en: Or set up new barriers to the ballot box.
sentences.zh: 或者为投票箱设置新的障碍。

sentences.en: Now, federal courts may strike these laws down as illegal.
sentences.zh: 现在，联邦法院可能会以违宪为由推翻这些法律。

sentences.en: That's certainly a possibility.
sentences.zh: 这当然是有可能的。

sentences.en: That's certainly a possibility.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是一种可能。

sentences.en: And congressional Democrats are trying to block them with a major voting rights bill in Congress, which has already passed the House,
sentences.zh: 国会民主党人正试图通过国会的一项重大投票权法案来阻止它们，该法案已经通过了众议院，

sentences.en: but faces a pretty uphill battle in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 但在参议院面临着相当艰难的阻力。

sentences.en: But the question of how successful these bills and laws will be for Republicans is a layered and kind of open-ended debate.
sentences.zh: 但这些法案和法律对共和党人来说究竟会有多成功，是一个多层面且有点开放式的辩论。

sentences.en: Let me just give you an example.
sentences.zh: 让我给你举个例子。

sentences.en: In the 2018 Georgia governor's race between Stacey Abrams and Brian Kemp, there was a host of actions taken by Governor Kemp, who at that point was Secretary of State,
sentences.zh: 在2018年佐治亚州州长竞选中，参选的斯泰西·艾布拉姆斯和布莱恩·坎普之间展开了对决，当时身为国务卿的坎普州长采取了一系列行动，

sentences.en: that was viewed as having an outsized impact on voters of color.
sentences.zh: 这些行动被认为对有色人种选民产生了过大的影响。

sentences.en: From purging voter rolls to delaying the registration of different voters whose names didn't perfectly match.
sentences.zh: 从清理选民名册到延迟那些名字不完全匹配的不同选民的登记。

sentences.en: And Stacey Abrams lost in a very close race and has since claimed that it was the result of these changes and voter suppression.
sentences.zh: 斯泰西·艾布拉姆斯在极为接近的竞选中落败，此后她声称这是这些变化和压制选民的结果。

sentences.en: And many Democrats believe that where Georgia is today is in part because of the energy and the motivation that the 2018 governor's race has brought to the base of the Democratic Party and the voters in Georgia.
sentences.zh: 许多民主党人认为，佐治亚州今天的局面部分要归功于2018年州长竞选给民主党基层和佐治亚州选民带来的活力和动力。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There's potentially a version of this where efforts to restrict Democratic voting ends up energizing Democratic voting in exactly the way Republicans did not intend.
sentences.zh: 可能存在这样一种情况：限制民主党人投票的努力，最终反而以共和党人意想不到的方式激发了民主党人的投票热情。

sentences.en: Yes, you could see almost any time a particular community's right to vote has been questioned or attempted to be restricted.
sentences.zh: 是的，几乎在任何时候，特定社群的投票权受到质疑或试图被限制时，你都能看到这一点。

sentences.en: It can be a motivating factor, an energizing factor.
sentences.zh: 这可能是一个激励因素，一个注入活力的因素。

sentences.en: And you wonder if the Republicans continue doing this in these battleground states, in these purple states, trying to restrict voting, could it completely backfire?
sentences.zh: 你禁不住想，如果共和党人继续在这些摇摆州、在这些紫色州这样做，试图限制投票，这会不会完全适得其反？

sentences.en: Could it actually animate the growing Democratic base there?
sentences.zh: 它会不会实际上激发出那里日益增长的民主党基层力量？

sentences.en: To turn out and flip these states blue.
sentences.zh: 让他们出来投票，把这些州变成蓝色。

sentences.en: And what will be the first big test of that question?
sentences.zh: 而对这个问题的第一个重大考验会是什么？

sentences.en: Whether or not these laws will help Republicans or help Democrats?
sentences.zh: 这些法律究竟会帮助共和党人还是帮助民主党人？

sentences.en: Well, looking ahead to the 2022 midterms, perhaps the most important state will be Georgia.
sentences.zh: 好吧，展望2022年中期选举，最重要的州也许会是佐治亚州。

sentences.en: It has a very highly anticipated governor's race where, although she hasn't necessarily said whether she intends to run or not,
sentences.zh: 那里的州长竞选备受瞩目，尽管她还没有明确表态自己是否打算参选，

sentences.en: Stacey Abrams is likely seen as challenging Governor Kemp again.
sentences.zh: 斯泰西·艾布拉姆斯预计仍将再次挑战坎普州长。

sentences.en: And you also have Senator Raphael Warnock, who is, again, the first black man to ever be elected senator from the state of Georgia in history,
sentences.zh: 你还有拉斐尔·沃纳克参议员，他同样是佐治亚州历史上第一位当选参议员的黑人男性，

sentences.en: up for a quick reelection after just winning in January against a Republican challenger.
sentences.zh: 在一月份刚刚击败共和党挑战者后，他很快将面临竞选连任。

sentences.en: So Georgia will again be at the top of the nation's attention and garnering among the most interest,
sentences.zh: 因此，佐治亚州将再次成为全国关注的焦点，并获得最多的兴趣、

sentences.en: most money and most outside support to kind of test whether these new laws will indeed have an impact benefiting one party or the other.
sentences.zh: 最多的资金和最多的外部支持，以此来检验这些新法律是否真的会产生有利于某一个政党的影响。

sentences.en: And so the first battleground state to pass these pretty sweeping voting restrictions since the 2020 election is likely to deliver the most meaningful verdict on which party they will ultimately benefit.
sentences.zh: 因此，自2020年大选以来第一个通过这些相当严厉的投票限制的摇摆州，很可能会对这些法律最终会使哪个政党受益做出最有意义的裁决。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Georgia is the state that raised the question for us here.
sentences.zh: 佐治亚州就是那个为我们提出这个问题的州。

sentences.en: And Georgia may indeed end up providing the answer.
sentences.zh: 而且佐治亚州最终也确实可能给出答案。

sentences.en: Nick, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 尼克，非常感谢。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Thanks, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: Tomorrow on The Daily, my colleague, Estet Herndon, speaks to Georgia Senator Raphael Warnock about his experience with voting rights and race.
sentences.zh: 明天的《每日新闻》节目中，我的同事埃斯特·赫登将与佐治亚州参议员拉斐尔·沃纳克交谈，探讨他关于投票权和种族的经历。

sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: And We plan to prove to you, beyond a reasonable doubt, that Mr. Chauvin was anything other than innocent on May 25th of 2020.
sentences.zh: 我们计划向你们毫无合理怀疑地证明，在2020年5月25日那天，肖万先生绝对不是无辜的。

sentences.en: On the first day of the murder trial of Derek Chauvin, the former Minneapolis police officer accused of killing George Floyd,
sentences.zh: 在前明尼阿波利斯警官德里克·肖万因涉嫌谋杀乔治·弗洛伊德而受审的第一天，

sentences.en: prosecutors said that witness testimony and video evidence would show that Chauvin's actions led to Floyd's death and were in no way the result of split-second judgments by an officer.
sentences.zh: 检方表示，证人证言和视频证据将表明，肖万的行为导致了弗洛伊德的死亡，绝不是一名警官在几分之一秒内做出的判断的结果。

sentences.en: This case is not about split-second decision-making.
sentences.zh: 这个案子不是关于瞬间决策的。

sentences.en: Finally, after six days, crews of diggers and a flotilla of tugboats successfully dislodged the 220,000-ton cargo ship from the muddy banks of the Suez Canal,
